note: Stage kits and Neglect places for the rule book. Tag format after the Without Number books: d6 each of Enemies, Friends, Complications, Things and Places. Names from the gazetteer are canon; everything else is table fodder until it's played.

stages.name: Market Square festival
blurb: Banners, awnings and stalls around a square megalith of grey volcanic stone carved with grim faces: one of the city's arches, and the busiest square in it. Traders from the Borderlands and from worlds through the arches sell food, gear and wonders at fair prices, and there is nearly always a festival on.
Jobs here are loud and quick. A crowd is cover, a festival is a timetable, and every stall is somebody's livelihood. Stage 1 is where heists go wrong in public and everyone ends up in the fountain.
stages.play: Run it as comedy with stakes. Chases knock over stalls, the crowd takes sides, and the worst outcome is being laughed out of the square, or arrested in front of it.
stages.canon: The megalith arch with grim faces; traders from the Borderlands and beyond the arches; the city's festivals (Celebration of the Found, Wolf Races, the Queen's High Day, Day of Sword and Fist).

stages.name: Villas of the Second Rise
blurb: Switchback roads climb from the city to a ridge of white villas pinned against the cliffs. Council members and the richest merchants live up here, behind the Silver Talons, a mercenary watch that answers to whoever pays the season's fee.

Nothing on the Second Rise is what it costs. Every house has a cellar older than the house, and a guest list that's really a list of debts. Jobs here are quiet: find what was lost before anyone notices, prove who did it without naming them, steal it back without breaking the glass.
stages.play: Run it as noir. Everyone is polite and everyone is lying about something small to hide something big. Violence is a scandal; a fight is loud, and the Silver Talons come.
stages.canon: Silver Talons (overseer Tanya Steelfang); Summervine Villa and Lady Elvenia Summervine (see the setting book's Summervine framework); the Reynold villa and the temple behind it.

stages.name: Public Baths and the Falls of the Three Gods
blurb: At the north edge of the city, three faceless statues two hundred feet tall catch glacial water in their hands and pour it, warmed, into a pool stepped like an upside-down pyramid. Half the city comes here to bathe, swim and talk business with nothing to hide behind.

The baths are where rumours are born and deals are struck without paper. Newly arrived folk are sent here by the Archkeepers to calm down. Under the pool, huge pipes carry the outflow down into the Lost Cisterns, and things sometimes come back up.
stages.play: Rumor and romance: everyone is unarmed, half-dressed and talking. The job is usually a conversation, and the fight, when it comes, comes up out of the water.
stages.canon: The Falls of the Three Sisters (Levyl, Kryssa and Dura, faceless gods of good), the Public Baths, the drains to the Lost Cisterns, the rumour of hollow statues (Gelered Stonehome's map).

stages.name: Cliffs of the Dead
blurb: West of the falls, the mountain is honeycombed with crypts, ossuaries, shrines and charnel pits, the oldest thousands of years deep. The Nameless King's magic twisted the veil here, so some of the dead don't rest, and the mountain slowly pulls its oldest tombs further in.

Tomb raiding is a crime, judged by the Magistrate of Tombs, a Council committee. It also licenses entry when an heir, preservation or a direct threat demands it. Stage 4 jobs are ghost stories with paperwork: who is allowed in, what they may carry out, and what follows them home.
stages.play: Ghost story: quiet, slow and sad before it is frightening. The dead want something specific, and the living usually want something they shouldn't have.
stages.canon: The Magistrate of Tombs and its licences; the Royal Tombs and their Golden Knight honour guard; the Arch of Threska; the Howling Catacombs and the corrupting spike; the Devouring Maw that draws old tombs deeper.

stages.name: Theater of Whispers
blurb: An open-air amphitheater older than anyone's records, free to all: plays every week, concerts every night, and bouts of non-lethal gladiatorial combat when the crowd wants blood that washes off. A gilded arch stands behind the stage, and now and then a stranger from another world steps through it in the middle of a show.

Under the stage a platform sinks on chains into halls of old props and older statues. The staff hear dead actors whispering their lines down there. Some say the vampires Vyctor and Evylend LeStrange, entertainers to the Nameless King, still keep their crypts below the lowest store.
stages.play: Masks and secrets: everyone has a role, and the job is to get someone to drop theirs. Scenes happen in front of a crowd that thinks it's part of the show.
stages.canon: Kaylex Thren, dragonborn master of revels; Bryessa Star, gnome singer; the under-theater and its thespian specters; Vyctor and Evylend LeStrange; the Night of the Dead play; the Whisper Company (Songweaver guild).

stages.name: Arch of Kings
blurb: The largest arch anyone knows of: two hundred feet of banded bronze-coloured stone, raised at the start of the Nameless King's reign and never opened. Every arrival sees it first. Under it is a plaza of pilgrims, hawkers, sages and zealots, all waiting for something.

Nobody agrees what's on the other side. Old texts say Choul, where the demon prince Ibraxus waits to step through. Others say the Outside, or the heavens. In Sejr every key in the city is a small door; this is the big one, and everyone with a theory wants to be the one holding the key when it turns.
stages.play: Run the weird straight. Arrivals are frightened and strange, prophets are sometimes right, and the arch should feel like it's listening.
stages.canon: Dennyse Alakamp's stolen ritual book and the mage Drakus (setting hook); the Choul, Outside and heavens theories; the Children of Ibraxus; the Archkeepers who greet arrivals.

neglect.name: Revlend Marshes
neglect.where: north and northwest: a hundred miles of lakes, pools and stilt villages
neglect.blurb: Revlenders fish, hunt and keep to themselves in stilt villages like Heron's Stride, trading fish in the city for everything else. Their seasonal festivals draw city folk out. Under the water lie drowned temples, barrows and the black dragon Rynfeyr's tower.
neglect.canon: Heron's Stride; Rynfeyr Blacktongue at Rynfeyr's Rest; Mirewraith's Barrow; Bloodrust Cove; the Tower of the Moons; Drowned Elvenya.
payoff: Refugees from a stilt village fill a holding's street, carrying their nets

neglect.name: Doorish Hills
neglect.where: south and southwest: a hundred miles of farmland, canals and small temples
neglect.blurb: The city's breadbasket: grain and cattle come in along the Suntouched Highway and the canals of Predalion's Belt. The Doorish keep many small temples to gods of food and fertility, and leave alone the tombs their eroding hills keep uncovering.
neglect.canon: Village of Peat; Predalion's Belt; the Suntouched Highway; Briarheart Forest and the Arch of Flowers; Sevelet's Throne and the Blood Spears; Castle Nightfall.

neglect.name: Deadlands
neglect.where: west: a hundred miles of dust, cracked earth and dead trees up to the Shattered Teeth
neglect.blurb: The Nameless King's mages tore the life out of this land. Caravans still cross it, and fewer arrive than set out. The walled City of Blades holds its edge, the Deadland Shadows keep the Oasis of Mother's Tears, and Vithra's idols stand in the dust.

neglect.name: Borderlands
neglect.where: the near country: the roads, walls and outskirts where the city meets the three lands
neglect.blurb: In the setting books the Borderlands are all three lands together. In Sejr this clock tracks the ring nearest the city: the gate roads, toll bridges, waystations and walled outskirts where marsh, hill and desert traffic meets the city's.
neglect.canon: The City Walls; the Suntouched Highway into the city; Borderlands traders in Market Square. The ring itself is this book's reading of the setting.

neglect.name: Lower Reaches
neglect.where: under the city: canals, everburning torches and miles of carved streets; also Stages 7-8
neglect.blurb: The city beneath the city, crossed by murky canals and lit by everburning torches. It isn't lawless, only flexible, and the Black Hand runs it from Mekello. The further from the centre, the more desolate the streets.
